description: List configured agent ids with name/model/runtime metadata, allowed as `sessions_spawn(runtime:"subagent")` targets.
name: agents_list

description: Send/manage channel messages. Supports actions: react, send. When the current WebChat prompt permits reactions, react with emoji (and optional remove:true) as the agent. Omit channel, target, and messageId. This stays local; use an explicit external channel and messageId for external reactions.

action.description: Select one action. For action="send", provide message or another send payload; fields for other actions do not count as send content.

asVoice.description: Send audio as a voice note; combines with voiceText.

emoji.description: One Unicode emoji for the current WebChat prompt; explicit external channels validate their own emoji.

final.description: For source replies, set false for progress; set true, or omit, for a completed send. For react, set true when adding a reaction to the current source message is your complete response; omit or set false when more work follows. A confirmed final source reply ends the turn.

forceDocument.description: Send media as document; no compression.

message.description: Text for action="send". A send needs message or another send payload such as media, attachments, or presentation.

message_id.description: snake_case alias of messageId; same defaults.

messageId.description: Target read/react/edit/delete/pin/unpin id; reactions default current inbound.

target.description: Recipient/channel: E.164 for WhatsApp/Signal, Telegram chat id/@username, Discord/Slack/Mattermost <channelId|user:ID|channel:ID>, or iMessage handle/chat_id

items.description: Recipient/channel targets (same format as --target); accepts ids or names when the directory is available.

trackToolCalls.description: Use the reacted message for this turn's status reaction lifecycle.

voiceText.description: Text to synthesize; message remains visible.

name: message

description: Spawn child session; default `runtime="subagent"`. `mode="run"` one-shot background. `agentId` targets a configured agent (see agents_list); `model` overrides its model; `cleanup` delete|keep hidden child session; `sandbox` inherit|require. Execute work directly by default. Delegate a bounded, independent task only when parallel execution or an independent review provides a concrete benefit. Keep dependent steps with the same owner. Once delegation is appropriate, use a hidden subagent unless the user needs to revisit or steer deliberately supervised child work. This includes substantial, bounded API/service investigations that can be handed off with the needed context and capabilities. For hidden subagents, omit `visible` or set it false, and report results through the parent. Native hidden or visible children support `worktree=true` with optional `projectId`, `worktreeName`, and `worktreeBaseRef`. Hidden `projectId` requires `worktree=true`; name/base always require it. Preparation is asynchronous; the first turn waits for the managed checkout. Hidden `cleanup=delete` uses session snapshot/removal; `keep` retains it. ACP does not support managed-worktree parameters. `group`, `projectGitUrl`, and cloud profiles require `visible=true`. `visible=true`: durable visible supervised child session. Use when the user needs to revisit or steer delegated child work; an explicit request for a new independent session is not child delegation. Shows in web UI sidebar; works without UI: announcing runs report back, progress checkable. `group` places it in a custom sidebar group (a new name creates the group); omission or an empty string leaves it ungrouped. Subagent only; omit `mode` (`mode="run"` is also accepted), `thread`, `thinking`, and `lightContext`; `attachments=[]` and omitted/blank `attachAs.mountPath` are accepted, but nonempty attachment staging is unsupported; inherits the caller tool-policy ceiling except for configured deny-only `delegateToolsTo` grants (not tool arguments); select a registered project with `projectId` or a managed GitHub clone with `projectGitUrl` (mutually exclusive with each other and `cwd`); may check out a git worktree via `worktree`/`worktreeName`/`worktreeBaseRef`. When its accepted result includes `sessionUrl`, channel acknowledgements put the session URL on the first line and `Owner: <label>` on the second line. Omit `placement` or use `{kind:"local"}` for local execution. `{kind:"profile",profileId,os?,machineClass?}` selects a configured cloud profile and requires `visible=true` and `worktree=true`. Cloud placement creates first, dispatches, then starts the task; failures retain the child for inspection, never fall back locally. Session listing/addressing obeys `tools.sessions.visibility` (all: all sessions, cross-agent per tools.agentToAgent).  Inherits parent workspace. Native task arrives in the child's initial `[Subagent Task]` message. Native: explicit context="isolated" starts clean; context="fork" copies requester transcript and requires the same agent. Omitted context is isolated. A PR/report, long runtime, or isolated worktree alone does not justify a sidebar session. A request for a subagent does not request a separate session. No spawn for quick lookup/single read. Check spawns via `subagents`/`sessions_history`. After spawn, do non-overlap work; follow the receipt's completion mode. When diagnosing a missing result from an announcing child, use `subagents` to inspect execution and delivery status. Recover existing results or follow up within the still-authorized task; respect intentional cancellation and never loop-poll.

attachAs.description: Attachment mount hint; visible=true accepts only an omitted or blank mountPath.

attachments.description: Inline snapshots; visible=true accepts only an empty array.

blind.description: Blind trial: child prompt omits its model, session ids and workspace path. Hidden subagent, context="isolated".

cleanup.description: Hidden session cleanup; delete snapshots and removes its managed worktree through session cleanup. visible=true always keeps the session.

completionTarget.description: parent: return substantive results in a private requester turn; no automatic channel delivery. After sessions_yield, the parent must receive the internal result even when no external reply is needed. For external replies only, exactly NO_REPLY as the entire final answer stays silent; a literal leading NO_REPLY newline suppresses that line only. NO_REPLY discards anything written this turn that was not sent, so send confirmations before ending silently. Native hidden run only; unavailable with ACP, collect, visible, thread, session mode, or expectsCompletionMessage=false.

context.description: Native: explicit context="isolated" starts clean; context="fork" copies requester transcript and requires the same agent. Omitted context is isolated.

cwd.description: Child working directory. Workspace-contained file tools (apply_patch/file writes) resolve and contain paths against cwd; set cwd for edits outside the agent workspace. Visible paths outside configured agent workspaces require operator.admin. Mutually exclusive with projectId/projectGitUrl. With no source selector and worktree=true: inherit the same-agent parent managed repository; otherwise use the target agent workspace.

cyberAccessProgram.description: Child OpenAI cyber Access (Blue=daybreak_blue, Red=daybreak_red). Omit: same-agent, same-model child keeps requester Access. Child run fails if its account/model lacks the program. Subagent only.

expectsCompletionMessage.description: false: fire-and-forget; requester gets no completion handoff when the child finishes.

group.description: Custom sidebar group; requires visible=true when nonempty. A new name creates the group. Omit or pass an empty string to leave it ungrouped.

label.description: Short task title shown in UI lists; name the work, not the agent.

lightContext.description: Light bootstrap; subagent only; unavailable with visible=true.

mode.description: "run" one-shot. Visible sessions accept omitted/default "run" and remain persistent.

placement.description: Execution placement: omitted or {kind: "local"} uses local execution for native and ACP runs. {kind: "profile", profileId, os?, machineClass?} selects a configured cloud profile and requires visible=true and worktree=true. Never supply placeholder selectors. Omitted cloud selectors use profile defaults; the first task starts only after cloud dispatch.

projectGitUrl.description: GitHub HTTPS or git@github.com repository URL for a visible session's managed clone; mutually exclusive with projectId and cwd. Local paths and file URLs are not accepted.

projectId.description: Registered project for a native subagent; hidden children require worktree=true. Mutually exclusive with projectGitUrl and cwd.

runtime.description: Runtime; visible=true and managed worktrees require "subagent".

runTimeoutSeconds.description: Child run timeout in seconds; overrides the configured subagent default and is preserved on native continuations. Zero disables the timeout; requester wake turns use their own budget.

sandbox.description: "inherit" parent sandbox policy; "require" fails unless child is sandboxed.

taskName.description: Stable later-target alias; starts lowercase letter; then lowercase/digit/_/-.

user.description: An admitted participant's requester_profile.id. Omit to use the turn's original requester; selection does not establish human intent or approval.

visible.description: Persistent sidebar session only when the user requests a separate session or needs to revisit and steer it independently. Internal QA/coding/review/test workers: omit or false. Subagent runtime only; default run mode and empty attachments accepted; no thread/thinking/lightContext or attachment staging.

worktree.description: Managed checkout for hidden or visible runtime="subagent"; first turn waits for preparation. ACP unsupported.

worktreeBaseRef.description: Managed worktree base ref; requires worktree=true.

worktreeName.description: Managed worktree lowercase slug, 1–64 letters/digits/hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. Do not include a branch prefix such as codex/; OpenClaw supplies openclaw/. Requires worktree=true.

name: sessions_spawn

tools.description:
Schedule reminders, delayed self-wakeups, recurring work, event watchers. Never exec sleep/poll as timer.

ACTIONS: status | list (enabled-only summaries by default; includeDisabled:true includes paused records; follow nextOffset) | get jobId (full details) | add job | update jobId job (partial; null clears) | remove jobId (operator removal requests active-run cancellation) | run jobId (runMode:"force"=now; waits up to timeoutMs, default 60s; unfinished runs return runId) | runs jobId runId? (history) | wake text (caller-owned session; mode defaults to next-heartbeat) | bind jobId (owner turn in the automation's parent conversation; links a key-only automation to this conversation). Check unfinished runs later with runs, never a scheduled verification job. wake has no delay; for a later resume use an at job below.

To pause a saved watcher without deleting its record, update job:{enabled:false}, or turn off its Active switch on the Automations page. The enabled flag and list absence do not prove source termination; use get jobId to inspect state.streamStatus.

SCOPE: Authenticated configured channel owners and Control UI administrators can manage any Gateway automation. Other turns see caller-visible jobs and scoped counts only: an empty list or failed list/get/update/remove (including not-found) does not establish global absence, even for IDs from your history. Never recreate or replace a known automation for update/remove/reconciliation based on these results; report the visibility limit and ask an authorized administrator to check through a fresh authenticated owner/administrator turn or the Automations page. New requested automations may still be created.

ADD: job requires name+schedule+payload.

WATCH OUTPUT: for continuous log monitoring and future alerts, add one saved stream directly. Example (replace the path with the requested log):
{action:"add",job:{name:"Application errors",schedule:{kind:"stream",command:["tail","-n","0","-F","<log path>"],mode:"match",match:"ERROR"},sessionTarget:"current",payload:{kind:"agentTurn",message:"Report the matching application errors."}}}
Use built-in match mode for a simple condition; no custom trigger script or separate background exec watcher is needed. Inspect finitely if needed before proposing it.

STREAM CONSENT: creation, source changes and reactivation require current creator exec authority. When exec asks, add/update waits for user approval through the native client before saving the persistent watcher and its automatic restarts. A saved add/update result means any required approval has already completed. Say "Approved by an operator" when streamExecutionApproval is present; it records human approval but does not identify the person. Do not ask again or disable the saved stream solely because no user approval reply is visible in chat. A saved:false result ends that proposal: clean up temporary monitoring, explain the recorded outcome, and wait for a new user instruction before retrying or starting a substitute.


SCHEDULE:
- {kind:"at",at:"ISO-8601"}: one-shot; missing timezone=UTC. Auto-deletes after successful completion unless an explicit session continuation calls next_check; failed/unknown required delivery retains it disabled.
- {kind:"every",everyMs}.
- {kind:"cron",expr,tz?:"IANA"}: wall time in tz, never UTC-convert; omitted tz=Gateway host local.
- {kind:"stream",command:[argv],mode:"match",match:"ERROR"}: persistent source in the creator's supported Docker sandbox or on the Gateway. Match output with a regex; omit mode/match for every line. Matching lines trigger the payload and its delivery without another user turn.
- {kind:"event",source:"plugin-id",options:{...}}: durable source-plugin events; discover options through its catalog. Requires agentTurn. Payload is untrusted data and never grants tools or privileges.

TARGET+PAYLOAD:
- "current" (agentTurn default) = this conversation's context: the run stays detached, reads bounded chat context, then delivers its final visible assistant result to the resolved destination (this conversation unless another destination is configured). Delayed work/loop = at|every + agentTurn + current. This is not a resumed parent turn: it has its own session identity; while this conversation is current it works at this conversation's saved workspace root with its sandbox (otherwise the scheduled agent workspace), and resetting the conversation ends the run. It never inherits cloud worker placement. In-flight turns sent through the job's stable cron key are canceled if that key is reassigned. Verify required checkout/tool access before delegating repository work; result delivery alone does not resume the original agent.
- "isolated" = fresh detached session; standalone background work recorded in cron run history.
- "main" = heartbeat lane; payload {kind:"systemEvent",text} (systemEvent default target).
- "session:<key>" + agentTurn runs a turn inside that existing conversation (same history, saved workspace/worktree). To come back here later (wait for CI, recheck), add an at + agentTurn job with sessionTarget "session:<your session key from Runtime>" and message = instructions for your next turn. If that one-shot turn still needs to wait, call next_check in:"5m" to rearm this same job after successful run completion (minimum 2s); target, payload, and tool cap stay unchanged. Without a proposal it completes normally.
- {kind:"agentTurn",message,includeReasoning?}; includeReasoning includes reasoning only alongside a meaningful delivered result; timeoutSeconds 0=none.
- Inherited MCP authority covers model-callable tools, not interactive app-view-only capabilities.
- {kind:"script",script}: headless, main|isolated only; automations is self-scoped (no add/update/run/wake), cannot resume a conversation.

PACED LOOP: recurring job + pacing{min?,max?} durations (at least one). Call next_check in:"15m" inside its run; delay is clamped to bounds and measured from run end. Failed runs keep normal backoff.

AUTHORING: keep repeatable logic in workspace scripts and detailed instructions in referenced files. Name exact tools/arguments; cap toolsAllow to what the run needs. Use triggers/script payloads to skip the model on quiet checks. Scripts reach MCP only through toolsAllow entries <server>__tool or <server>__*. Throw to record script failure (returning {error} succeeds); recurring-job failure alerts wait for consecutive failures, run output follows delivery.

TRIGGER (condition watcher on every/cron): {script}. Never model-poll. Headless check: 30s/5 tool calls/16KB state. Read frozen trigger.state; return json({fire,message?,state?}) with new state for dedupe. fire:false saves state without a model call; fire:true runs payload with self-contained message. Fire on failures/timeouts too. Keep checks read-only; actions belong in payload. once:true disables after first fire. Code Mode: await exec({command:"..."}).

DELIVERY: omitted=announce. Agent, command, and script jobs send their final visible result to the destination, then add confirmed delivery once to that conversation, independently of isolated/current/persistent execution. Set channel/to/accountId/threadId to select another destination; the creating conversation is the fallback when no external route exists. Verified matching message-tool delivery suppresses the notification resend, not the conversation result. Failed or uncertain external sends are not added to conversation history; a failed history write after confirmed delivery records a warning without failing delivery. With no external route, the conversation commit completes delivery and appears live and after reconnect. Use none for no automatic result or notification.  Silent watcher=>mode:"none". webhook posts finished-run event (successful empty summary is intentional silence, no POST) to URL in `to`. To keep announce delivery and also POST completion, use mode:"announce" with completionDestination:{mode:"webhook",to:"https://..."}.

FAILURE ALERTS: routed jobs default to 2 consecutive execution failures and 1h cooldown; terminal one-shot failures bypass that count. failureAlert:false disables execution/delivery alerts, not auto-disable notices. bestEffort suppresses inherited execution alerts. Required-delivery failures use an alternate route, bypass after, and share the cooldown without incrementing the execution streak.

Optional job policy: activeHours{start,end,timezone?} is an end-exclusive execution window (including manual runs); idleOnly yields to foreground work. delivery.target:"owner" resolves the owner DM dynamically, never the last group; delivery.directPolicy:"block" prohibits DMs. agentTurn skipIfScratchEmpty skips an explicitly empty checklist, not missing scratch.

Main-job wakeMode: "now"(default)|"next-heartbeat". contextMessages 0-10 embeds recent chat lines in reminder text.

Inside a scheduled run only: Inspect or remove only the current automation. Actions: status; list [includeDisabled] (enabled only by default); get/runs/remove jobId. Use get with the current job ID to inspect its saved state. To stop a finished job, remove it; creating/updating/running jobs and waking sessions are unavailable. Return the task result; the scheduler owns delivery. scratch_get reads this job's checklist and revision; scratch_set replaces or clears content using expectedRevision from the read (reread after a revision conflict). record_result accepts one outcome (no_change, progress, done, blocked, needs_attention). Omit summary for no_change; other outcomes require a trimmed 1–2000-character summary. Unchanged state and repeated known blockers stay quiet with no_change and NO_REPLY; explicit recurring digests/reports still deliver as requested. Use existing deterministic condition triggers or scripts to skip inference for machine-checkable no-change. no_change or NO_REPLY keeps the response silent. next_check in:"15m" proposes the next delay for this paced job or one-shot session continuation. A successful one-shot proposal rearms this same job from run end (minimum 2s); without one it completes normally.

agentId.description: List filter for `action: "list"`; wake target override for `action: "wake"` (defaults to the calling agent when omitted on wake)

includeDisabled.description: List: false by default; true includes disabled saved jobs.

job.description: Job fields. action="add": full job. action="update": partial patch — only supplied fields change; null clears.

declarationKey.description: Key to avoid duplicate declarations (add only).

deleteAfterRun.description: Delete one-shot after successful completion: delivery confirmed, not requested, intentionally silent, or explicitly bestEffort. Failed/unknown required delivery retains it disabled.

accountId.description: Delivery account, or null to clear

bestEffort.description: Omitted/false requires requested delivery for successful completion; true lets successful execution complete and delete a one-shot despite failed/unknown delivery. Intentional silence succeeds in either mode.

channel.description: Delivery channel, or null to clear

to.description: Completion webhook target; only valid with delivery.mode=announce

completionDestination.description: Completion webhook; requires delivery.mode=announce; null clears.

accountId.description: Failure delivery account, or null to clear

channel.description: Failure delivery channel, or null to clear

to.description: Failure delivery target, or null to clear

failureDestination.description: Failure-alert route override; required-delivery failures bypass after but share the execution-alert cooldown; null clears.

to.description: Delivery target, or null to clear

after.description: Consecutive execution failures before alert; delivery failures bypass this threshold

failureAlert.description: Failure alert policy/route override; null clears. Route-backed jobs default to after=2 for execution failures and cooldownMs=3600000 for all failure alerts; false disables execution/delivery alerts but not the auto-disable safety notice.

anyOf.description: Dynamic-cadence bounds; at least one of min or max is required

allowUnsafeExternalContent.description: Allow untrusted external content in prompt

fallbacks.description: Fallback models, or null to clear

includeReasoning.description: Include reasoning with a meaningful delivered result

lightContext.description: Lightweight bootstrap context (skip full workspace context)

model.description: Model override, or null to clear

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout seconds; null restores the default on update (omission preserves it)

toolsAllow.description: Allowed tool ids, or null to clear

command.description: Supervised source argv (kind=stream; disabled when cron.triggers.enabled=false)

expr.description: Cron wall-time expr; never UTC-convert. Missing tz preserves the existing cron timezone on update; otherwise Gateway local. Example "0 18 * * *", "Asia/Shanghai".

match.description: Regex source for mode=match, e.g. ERROR; matching output is appended to the payload

mode.description: Stream output: line accepts every line; match uses the match regex without a trigger script

options.description: Event source options from its plugin catalog (kind=event)

tz.description: IANA timezone for wall-clock fields. Omit on update to preserve the existing cron timezone; otherwise defaults to Gateway host local timezone. Example "Asia/Shanghai".

sessionKey.description: Explicit session key, or null to clear it

offset.description: Job offset for action="list"; use nextOffset to load the next page

runId.description: Run id from action="run" to read with action="runs"

runMode.description: Run mode for action="run": omitted defaults to "due"; use "force" to trigger now.

sessionKey.description: Wake target override for `action: "wake"`: route the event to another session owned by the calling agent. Defaults to the resolved calling-session key when omitted.

tools.name: automations

tools.description: Read gateway config/schema. Owner request/operator schedule: update.run, restart, update.cleanup. Use runtime-owned actions. Other system changes: use openclaw tool.

dryRun.description: update.cleanup only: preview without removing recovery copies.

note.description: Short human note for the update or post-restart notice.

path.description: Required for config.schema.lookup; optional for config.get.

tools.name: gateway

tools.description: Discover, configure, and control paired devices, including computers, phones, watches, dials, relays, and sensors. Use status to find nodes, describe to inspect advertised commands, and invoke for custom device commands. Status includes active-computer presence. Pairing lifecycle (pending/approve/reject), notify, camera_snap/camera_list/camera_clip (with audio), camera_ptz for physical camera pan/tilt/zoom, photos_latest, screen_snapshot, screen_record video, location_get, notifications_list + notifications_action (open/dismiss/reply), device_status/device_info/device_permissions/device_health, executable lookup (which + bins), generic invoke (fs.listDir returns sub-directories only). File transfer is a separate capability.

bins.description: which: executable names to resolve on the selected node.

deviceId.description: For camera_ptz, use a camera_list devices[].id value as deviceId; it is required and must not be guessed.

invokeCommand.description: Node command to relay. fs.listDir returns sub-directories only.

node.description: Node ID, name, or IP. Required for describe and node-targeted actions; use status to discover nodes.

panDegrees.description: camera_ptz pan: set uses absolute degrees; move uses a degree delta. Omit when unsupported.

ptzOperation.description: camera_ptz operation. Call status before any control operation. status and home accept no axes; set uses absolute axes; move uses axis deltas. Never guess unsupported axes.

tiltDegrees.description: camera_ptz tilt: set uses absolute degrees; move uses a degree delta. Omit when unsupported.

zoomPercent.description: camera_ptz zoom: set uses absolute percent; move uses a percentage-point delta. Omit when unsupported.

tools.name: nodes

tools.description: Show visible-session model/usage/time/cost/tasks. `sessionKey="current"` for current; UI labels are not keys. `model` overrides; `model=default` resets. Use for active model/session questions. `capabilities=true` lists this session's available tools and why others are missing.

user.description: An admitted participant's requester_profile.id. Omit to use the turn's original requester; selection does not establish human intent or approval.

tools.name: session_status

tools.description: Read sanitized visible-session history. Before reply/debug/resume. Use messageId for anchored history; sessionId selects its transcript and requires messageId. Omit both for the latest tail. offset pages unanchored history and is ignored with messageId. limit bounds either mode. Include tool messages with includeTools. pendingInputs are accepted inputs outside model history; page with pendingBefore=nextBefore. Cancelled inputs never replay; interrupted means saved without an active retry. Eligible durable peer sends can regain queued custody on startup. Lower limit for richer pending previews.

messageId.description: Return history around this message id. Ignores offset; limit bounds the window.

offset.description: Plain-pagination offset. Ignored when messageId is set; limit still bounds anchored history.

sessionId.description: Transcript session id that owns messageId. Requires messageId; omit for the latest tail.

user.description: An admitted participant's requester_profile.id. Omit to use the turn's original requester; selection does not establish human intent or approval.

tools.name: sessions_history

tools.description: List visible session metadata and groups; filter ownerId/creatorId, projectId/workspaceDir, group/pinned, kind/agent/activity/archive. relationship=owned|created|involving selects the authenticated requesting user's sessions, not the agent's owner. Metadata-only by default. limit defaults to 100; larger requests stay valid but limitApplied never exceeds 200. count is this page, not an inventory total. Continue with nextOffset and identical filters while hasMore; truncationReason names a scan/byte budget. Pages are live: deduplicate by agentId/key/sessionId or restart for a fresh inventory. archived=all includes active and archived rows. Preview recent messages inline via includeLastMessage/messageLimit; includeDerivedTitles adds derived titles. enrichmentOmitted means previews exceeded the byte budget; read history separately. Run outcomes: `done` means success, `failed` error, `timeout` time limit, and `killed` cancellation. These describe the last run, not task completion or whether the session can continue. Before spawning replacement work, consider a same-session follow-up; it still requires current access and lifecycle checks to admit new work. Use before history/send target selection.

relationship.description: Relation to the authenticated requesting user; unavailable without a trusted user identity.

user.description: An admitted participant's requester_profile.id. Omit to use the turn's original requester; selection does not establish human intent or approval.

tools.name: sessions_list

tools.description: Search visible past sessions for matching user and assistant text. Follow up with sessions_history using a returned sessionKey, sessionId, and messageId for neighboring context.

query.description: Required non-empty keywords to match in past user and assistant text.

user.description: An admitted participant's requester_profile.id. Omit to use the turn's original requester; selection does not establish human intent or approval.

tools.name: sessions_search

tools.description: Send a message to a permitted session on this Gateway by sessionKey/label, or a configured local agent by agentId; sessionKey wins redundant label. Explicit per-agent send destinations can permit messaging without transcript access. A session identifies model context, not an external address. When a new turn starts, its reply reaches you once: inline when available, otherwise as a later inter-session input. Continue with another sessions_send; post to channels with message. Accepted results report target admission as `targetDisposition: "queued"` or `"steered"`; `delivery.status` is only later reply delivery state, and neither proves target completion. Omit mode to automatically continue your paused native child task; returns runId/taskRunId with task-owned completion instead of an inline wait or watch. Ordinary peer sends start a separate turn. A zero-wait send to your own busy child or an eligible run-scoped target may use its active input queue. An idle recipient or a default self-send starts a new turn; timeoutSeconds bounds waiting for the separately admitted turn’s reply. mode:notify queues ephemeral context for the next turn without waking or starting work (bounded process memory, not a durable inbox). mode:steer injects guidance into an active supported run and never starts idle work. mode:followup always starts a separate turn and preserves its independent reply; it does not resume a paused task. mode:resume requires a paused native child task and rejects watch:true and positive timeoutSeconds. For an exact external destination, use `conversations_list` plus `conversations_send`/`conversations_turn`. Thread chats rejected: target parent channel. Missing configured-agent main created. status "no_reply" is terminal, so do not wait for another reply. A timeoutSeconds:0 send that starts a new turn for your existing native child gives this turn a completion to await with sessions_yield, even while queued. watch:true requires status visibility and additionally reports later target-session changes; on a steer it can claim the child's existing pending completion.

user.description: An admitted participant's requester_profile.id. Omit to use the turn's original requester; selection does not establish human intent or approval.

tools.name: sessions_send

tools.description: List native subagents, wait for selected runIds, or cancel a runId and its descendants. A wait timeout never cancels execution or consumes completion delivery.

timeoutSeconds.description: Wait duration in integer seconds, 0–60 (default: 30). Use 0 for a snapshot.

tools.name: subagents

tools.description: Convert text to spoken audio (TTS) with the configured voice provider. Only explicit voice/speech/TTS intent or active TTS config; never ordinary text reply. Audio auto-delivered. After success follow reply instructions; no duplicate text/audio.
tools.name: tts

tools.description: Fetch URL; extract readable markdown/text. Lightweight; no browser automation.
tools.name: web_fetch

tools.description: Search current web; normalized provider results. Supports freshness and date-range filters (freshness, date_after/date_before) and domain filtering (domain_filter).
tools.name: web_search

tools.description: End this turn to await pending child completions, not submit a final result. Return completed work normally. Does not message other sessions. Omit waitFor when yielding for your own children; their completions resume this session. Set waitFor:"message" only when a subagent has no pending children and waits for its requester to send it a continuation. For background tools, follow their continuation instructions. Automation turns end here; the scheduler delivers child output under the job delivery policy. Collector runs require explicit collection instead.

acknowledgment.description: Optional brief waiting status shown to the user as your message; put answers in normal assistant text. With waitFor, also the task pause notice. Not an inter-session message.

message.description: Private context for the resumed turn; not sent to the user.

waitFor.description: Only for a subagent with no pending children of its own that waits for its requester to send it a continuation. Omit when yielding for your own children: their completions resume this session. Does not send or schedule that message or submit a final result.

tools.name: sessions_yield
